# AGENTS.md

These instructions apply to all AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.), not just one tool.

## Workflow

Follow PIV: **Plan** first (write the plan, don't touch code) → **Implement** per the plan →
**Verify** (lint, typecheck, test) before declaring done. If verify fails, fix it and
retry (max 3x); if it still fails, stop and escalate to a human.

This project's ticket tracker: **Linear**. Artifact folder names
follow the ticket key (`ENG-123`, `#42`, etc.), consistent with the branch name
`ai-agent/{{TICKET-ID}}`.

- Don't auto-generate the contents of `.caf/knowledge/golden-examples/` or `.caf/knowledge/decisions/` —

# .caf/tasks/

> **DRAFT — must be reviewed.** This file was auto-generated by `caf-initiator`.

Each ticket gets its own folder here. Agents hand off files to each other, not chat/memory.

Folder names follow the ticket key from the tracker (**Linear**),
consistent with the branch name `ai-agent/{{TICKET-ID}}`.

## Structure per Ticket

```
.caf/tasks/{{TICKET-ID}}/
  requirements.md    ← Planner Agent: what's requested, acceptance criteria
  design.md          ← Architect Agent: technical approach (if needed)
  tasks.md           ← Planner Agent: concrete task breakdown
  verify-report.md   ← implementation agent: implementation + verify results
  qa-report.md       ← QA Agent: deep test results
  review-notes.md    ← Reviewer Agent: qualitative review results
```

See `CAF.md` Layer 3 for the `verify-report.md` format and details on each artifact.

# Run Pipeline (Manual, No Orchestrator)

**This command WRITES CODE and CREATES A BRANCH.** It's the only command generated by
caf-initiator that does both — treat it more carefully than the others.

Purpose: a manual alternative for projects that haven't set up (or don't want) `caf-orchestrator`
(webhook + VPS). The flow mirrors the automated pipeline, including **auto-commit, auto-push, and
auto `gh pr create`** after Reviewer APPROVE — see section 7. No ticket status is changed in the
tracker (that stays manual); only git + PR are automated.

**If it stops at NEEDS_HUMAN** (implementation, QA gate, or Reviewer gate): there is NO commit,
push, or PR at all — the working tree is left as-is on branch `ai-agent/{TICKET-ID}` for a human.
See "Controlled Stop" below.

Boundary worth knowing: the `allowed-tools` allowlist above binds this command (MAIN THREAD),
**not the spawned subagents** — subagents run with the tools from their own agent definition.
That's why every spawn prompt below MUST explicitly include the push/PR prohibition ("that's the
main thread's job in section 7, not yours") — commit/push/PR may happen only once, in section 7,
performed by the main thread after all gates pass.

## Ticket

Ticket ID: `$ARGUMENTS`

Required. If empty, ask the user which ticket is meant and STOP until answered — don't guess.

Fetch ticket details (title, description, acceptance criteria): if a tracker MCP is connected
(Linear/Jira/GitHub Issues), use it. Otherwise, ask the user to paste the ticket details manually
before continuing — don't invent requirements that weren't stated.

## 0. Guard — required, before spawning anything

Run these four checks **sequentially and to completion** before the Task tool is used at all.
Don't spawn any agent "while waiting for the user's answer".

### 0.1 Working directory must be clean

`git status --porcelain`. If there's output (uncommitted changes) → **STOP**, show the list, ask
the user to commit/stash first. Don't check out a new branch with changes that could get carried
along or lost.

### 0.2 Does branch `ai-agent/{TICKET-ID}` already exist?

Check **both local AND remote** — both, not just one:

```
git branch --list ai-agent/{TICKET-ID}
git ls-remote --heads origin ai-agent/{TICKET-ID}
```

Checking remote isn't a formality: `caf-orchestrator` runs on a VPS, so if it has already/is
currently handling this ticket, its branch shows up on the **remote** and may not exist in the
user's working copy at all. A local-only check would pass exactly in the most dangerous case.

If this repo has no `origin` remote at all (`git ls-remote` fails with "'origin' does not appear
to be a git repository"), that's **not a guard failure** — a purely local repo simply can't be
claimed by the orchestrator. Note "remote: none", proceed with the local check result only. Don't
STOP because of this, and don't treat the remote check as passed either.

- **Not present in either** → proceed to 0.3.
- **Present in either/both** → **STOP**. This is a strong signal this ticket is already/currently
  being handled by the orchestrator or a previous `/caf-run-pipeline` run. Show the user:
  - `git log --oneline` for that branch (whatever commits already exist there),
  - the contents of `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/verify-report.md` if it exists,
  - whether it was local, remote, or both.

  Then ask for explicit confirmation: **continue on that branch**, or **abort**. DO NOT assume
  it's safe to continue, and DO NOT create a new branch that overwrites it. If the user chooses
  to continue, `git checkout ai-agent/{TICKET-ID}` (not `-b`).

  **Limitation you must disclose to the user at this point:** an orchestrator run that just
  started and hasn't pushed its branch yet is NOT detected by this check. If the user knows an
  automated pipeline is currently running for this ticket, abort — regardless of the check
  results above.

### 0.3 Already completed before?

Check `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/verify-report.md`.

If that file exists and its status is **not** `NEEDS_HUMAN` → **STOP**. This ticket has likely
already been completed. Show its summary, ask the user: **restart from scratch (override)** or
**abort**. Don't silently overwrite completed work.

Deliberately phrased as "not NEEDS_HUMAN" rather than "equals SUCCESS": the success label in
`verify-report.md` isn't consistent across sources (CAF.md calls it `SUCCESS`, the handoff
template calls it `PASS`, and agents in the wild sometimes write `DONE`). The only consistent
marker is `NEEDS_HUMAN` for "not yet done". Matching the exact string `SUCCESS` would make this
guard silently never fire — exactly the failure it's meant to prevent.

If the status is `NEEDS_HUMAN`, don't STOP: this ticket was genuinely left unfinished. Tell the
user this run continues previously interrupted work, then proceed.

### 0.4 Create the branch

Only after 0.1-0.3 pass: `git checkout -b ai-agent/{TICKET-ID}` from the currently active branch.
If the user already chose "continue" in 0.2, the branch is already checked out — skip this step.

## 1. Planner (required)

Spawn Planner. Its source of truth is `.claude/agents/caf-planner.md` — read that file and follow
it. Input: ticket details from the Ticket section above.

Required output: `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/requirements.md` and `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/tasks.md`.

If Planner reports the ticket is too ambiguous to break down, **STOP the entire pipeline** —
report to the user and ask for ticket clarification. Don't proceed to implementation with a plan
Planner itself says it isn't confident about.

## 2. Architect (conditional)

This stage is **conditional** — don't always spawn it.

Spawn Architect (`.claude/agents/caf-architect.md`) ONLY if either is true:

- `tasks.md` from Planner explicitly states it needs an architecture/design decision, OR
- the task touches more than one app/service, OR involves a new schema/migration.

If the ticket is simple and single-app, **skip** — go on to stage 3. Producing `design.md`
for a task that doesn't need it just adds run cost and a document nobody reads.

Output: `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/design.md`. If skipped, note in the final summary that this
stage was skipped along with the reason — don't let it silently disappear from the report.

## 3. Implementation

Implementation agents available in this project:

- `caf-frontend` (`.claude/agents/caf-frontend.md`)
- `caf-backend` (`.claude/agents/caf-backend.md`)

**How to choose which agent to spawn** (this decision must NOT be guessed):

1. Read the app/module column of each task in `tasks.md`.
2. Match it against each agent's scope above — read `## Scope` in the agent's file, don't
   guess from its name.
3. A task whose app/module matches one agent's scope → that agent handles it.
4. If a task doesn't match any agent's scope, OR matches more than one, **ask the user**
   which agent should handle it and STOP until answered.
   Misrouting means an agent writes code outside its scope — a silent failure only caught at
   review time.
5. An agent with no tasks at all: DO NOT spawn it. Not a failure — there's simply no work for
   it on this ticket.

If multiple agents have tasks, run them **sequentially, not in parallel** — both write to the
same working tree. Order follows the task dependencies in `tasks.md`.

Input for each agent: `requirements.md`, `tasks.md`, and `design.md` if stage 2 ran.

Every spawn prompt MUST include, verbatim:

> Do not `git push`, do not open a PR, do not change the ticket status in the tracker — that is the main thread's job in section 7, not yours. Write only the code and
> `verify-report.md`, on the branch that's already active.

**Internal PIV is that agent's own concern.** Implementation agents already have their own Retry
Logic (implement → verify → fix, max 3x) in their definition. You are **NOT** allowed to respawn
an implementation agent just because its verify failed — that would effectively double the retry
budget. The only respawn path is the gate retries in stages 5 and 6.

If an agent finishes with `verify-report.md` `Status: NEEDS_HUMAN`:
**STOP the entire pipeline here.** Don't proceed to Documentation/QA/Reviewer with code whose
verify hasn't passed — every subsequent stage would produce a report about code already known to
be broken, and that's wasted cost.

## 4. Documentation (non-blocking)

This project has no Documentation Agent (`.claude/agents/caf-documentation.md` was not
generated) — skip this stage, note "not available" in the final summary. This is not a
pipeline failure.

## 5. QA (gate)

The QA (`.claude/agents/caf-qa.md`) spawn prompt MUST include, verbatim:

> Do not `git push`, do not open a PR, do not change the ticket status in the tracker — that is the main thread's job in section 7, not yours.

**Gate — `qaRetryCount`, `MAX_QA_RETRIES = 1`.**

Set `qaRetryCount = 0` at the start of this run. This counter is **fresh every time
`/caf-run-pipeline` runs** and **independent** of other gate counters — budget exhausted on
one gate does NOT reduce another gate's budget. Don't treat it as a shared budget.

Flow:

1. Spawn QA (`.claude/agents/caf-qa.md`), wait for its result.
2. Result OK → proceed to the next stage.
3. Result `NEEDS_HUMAN / has a CRITICAL issue`:
   - If `qaRetryCount >= MAX_QA_RETRIES` → **STOP here**, report NEEDS_HUMAN (see
     "Controlled Stop" below).
   - Otherwise → increment `qaRetryCount` by 1 from its previous value, then **respawn the
     relevant implementation agent** with `qa-report.md` as input, asking it to fix only the
     findings (not redo the implementation from scratch). Once the fix is done, run this gate
     **once more**, back to step 1.
4. Budget exhausted (`qaRetryCount >= MAX_QA_RETRIES`) and the gate still fails → STOP,
   NEEDS_HUMAN.

Retry means **fix, then re-check** — not running the gate twice over the exact same code.
Re-running the gate with nothing changed just burns cost for a result that's already certain to
be the same.

A `NON-CRITICAL` issue found by QA does NOT fail the gate — that's intentional, not an
overlooked gap. If QA closes with `## Status: PASS` while the `### NON-CRITICAL` section in
`qa-report.md` is non-empty, treat it as "Result OK" and proceed to the next stage. Those
findings stay recorded in `qa-report.md` to be addressed separately — outside this retry loop.
Only `## Status: NEEDS_HUMAN` or content in the `### CRITICAL` section triggers the retry
gate.

Artifact: `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/qa-report.md`.

## 6. Reviewer (gate)

The Reviewer (`.claude/agents/caf-reviewer.md`) spawn prompt MUST include, verbatim:

> Do not `git push`, do not open a PR, do not change the ticket status in the tracker — that is the main thread's job in section 7, not yours.

**Gate — `reviewerRetryCount`, `MAX_REVIEWER_RETRIES = 1`.**

Set `reviewerRetryCount = 0` at the start of this run. This counter is **fresh every time
`/caf-run-pipeline` runs** and **independent** of other gate counters — budget exhausted on
one gate does NOT reduce another gate's budget. Don't treat it as a shared budget.

Flow:

1. Spawn Reviewer (`.claude/agents/caf-reviewer.md`), wait for its result.
2. Result OK → proceed to the next stage.
3. Result `REQUEST_CHANGES / NEEDS_HUMAN`:
   - If `reviewerRetryCount >= MAX_REVIEWER_RETRIES` → **STOP here**, report NEEDS_HUMAN (see
     "Controlled Stop" below).
   - Otherwise → increment `reviewerRetryCount` by 1 from its previous value, then **respawn the
     relevant implementation agent** with `review-notes.md` (BLOCKING findings only) as input, asking it to fix only the
     findings (not redo the implementation from scratch). Once the fix is done, run this gate
     **once more**, back to step 1.
4. Budget exhausted (`reviewerRetryCount >= MAX_REVIEWER_RETRIES`) and the gate still fails → STOP,
   NEEDS_HUMAN.

Retry means **fix, then re-check** — not running the gate twice over the exact same code.
Re-running the gate with nothing changed just burns cost for a result that's already certain to
be the same.

Artifact: `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/review-notes.md`.

To be explicit: `reviewerRetryCount` is **not affected** by what happens in the QA stage. A
ticket whose QA passed after a retry still enters this stage with a full budget of 1.

## 7. Commit, Push, PR (SUCCESS)

**This stage runs ONLY if Reviewer APPROVEs.** If the pipeline stopped at any stage before this
(implementation NEEDS_HUMAN, QA/Reviewer gate exhausted), **skip this entire section** and go
straight to "Controlled Stop" below — don't commit anything.

Run these seven steps **in order**. Any step with a STOP condition must halt there, not proceed
to the next step — a commit with the wrong scope or a push that collides with the remote branch
can't easily be undone once it happens.

### 7.1 Scope whitelist

Paths allowed into the commit (ONLY these, not the entire working tree):

- `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/` (artifact)
- `caf-frontend`: `apps/web/`
- `caf-backend`: `apps/api/`

`git status --porcelain` → match **every** changed path against the whitelist above.

A path changed BUT not in any whitelist → **STOP, DO NOT commit anything**. Show the suspicious
paths to the user, explain this is likely a file outside the assigned agent's scope (a bug or
scope creep in a subagent). Ask the user to decide manually — commit anyway after verifying, or
investigate first. In the Final Summary, record the status as "SUCCESS but commit aborted —
scope drift detected", not a plain SUCCESS status.

### 7.2 Commit

`git add --` followed by the explicit list of paths from 7.1 that actually changed (**not**
`git add -A`), then:

```
git commit -m "AI agent pipeline: {TICKET-ID}"
```

Without `--allow-empty`. If the commit fails because there's nothing to commit ("nothing to
commit") — that's an odd signal (implementation reported done but there's no diff at all) →
**STOP**, report to the user, don't proceed to push/PR.

### 7.3 Guard — fetch before push

```
git fetch origin ai-agent/{TICKET-ID}
```

If fetch fails because the branch doesn't exist on the remote at all, that's not a guard
failure — proceed treating it as "remote doesn't exist yet" (next step).

- **Remote doesn't exist** → safe, proceed to 7.4.
- **Remote exists**, and `git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/ai-agent/{TICKET-ID} HEAD`
  succeeds (exit 0) → the remote SHA is an ancestor of local HEAD, safe, proceed to 7.4.
- **Remote exists**, and `git merge-base --is-ancestor` fails (exit != 0) → the remote SHA is
  NOT an ancestor of local HEAD. **STOP before pushing.** This signals the remote branch has been
  changed by another party (the orchestrator, or another `/caf-run-pipeline` run) since guard
  0.2 ran at the start of this command. Show the user: the remote SHA, `git log --oneline` of
  that remote branch, and the local commit just created in 7.2 (still in the working tree, not
  yet pushed). **DO NOT force-push, DO NOT auto merge/rebase** — that's a human decision.

**Limitation to disclose to the user at this point**: this is best-effort, not an absolute
guarantee — a race condition between this fetch-check and the push in 7.4 is still possible
(small window, but real) if another party pushes exactly between the two steps. There's no
distributed lock available from this command's side to close that gap entirely — same pattern of
limitation as guard 0.2.

### 7.4 Push

```
git push --set-upstream origin ai-agent/{TICKET-ID}
```

### 7.5 Detect base branch

```
gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef --jq .defaultBranchRef.name
```

Save the result as `{BASE-BRANCH}`. **Don't hardcode `main`** — the target repo might use
`master`, `develop`, or another name.

### 7.6 Check for an existing PR (idempotency)

```
gh pr list --head ai-agent/{TICKET-ID} --state open --json url,number
```

- **Result found** → a PR for this branch already exists (e.g. opened manually by the user after
  a previous NEEDS_HUMAN run, and now the follow-up run succeeded). **Don't** call
  `gh pr create` — the push in 7.4 already updates the branch underlying that PR. Take the URL
  from the `gh pr list` result, note it for the Final Summary as "PR already exists, branch
  updated" — not an error.
- **Empty** → proceed to 7.7.

### 7.7 `gh pr create`

Title:
```
{TICKET-ID}: {ticket title from the Ticket section}
```

Body — structure identical to `buildPrBody` in caf-orchestrator (`run-agent-pipeline.use-case.ts`),
so both execution paths produce the same PR shape:

```
Ticket: {TICKET-ID}
{ticket description from the Ticket section}

## Reports
- Requirements: `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/requirements.md`
- Verify: `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/verify-report.md`
- QA: `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/qa-report.md`
- Review: `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/review-notes.md`

{docsNote — Documentation status from stage 4: SUCCESS / FAILED (non-blocking) / NOT AVAILABLE,
the equivalent wording already used in the Final Summary}

{raw contents of qa-report.md}

{raw contents of review-notes.md}
```

No skip-gate warning block (`qualityGateWarning` in the orchestrator) — this command has no
skip-QA/Reviewer feature, so it's not applicable.

Base: `{BASE-BRANCH}` from 7.5. Save the URL returned by `gh pr create` for the Final Summary.

## Controlled Stop (NEEDS_HUMAN)

If any gate exhausts its budget, or implementation ends in NEEDS_HUMAN: that's a **controlled
stop, not an error**. Don't throw an exception, don't make the command look like it "crashed",
don't try an alternative path not instructed here.

What to do: stop at that stage, go straight to the Final Summary with status NEEDS_HUMAN and
state which stage stopped it plus what findings remain unresolved. Code already written stays on
the branch — don't revert it, don't delete it. A human decides whether to continue or discard it.

**To be explicit: the NEEDS_HUMAN path never reaches section 7.** There is no commit, push, or PR
at all on this path — the working tree is left exactly as the last stage that stopped the
pipeline left it. This isn't new behavior (it's already implied by the stop/`return` structure
in each gate), written explicitly here to remove ambiguity.

## Verify

Before writing the final summary, confirm with Bash/Read — not from memory of the flow.

**If the run ended NEEDS_HUMAN:**

- [ ] The currently active branch really is `ai-agent/{TICKET-ID}` (`git branch --show-current`)
- [ ] The artifact for every stage that ran actually exists in `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/`
- [ ] **No push happened** — `git status -sb`: the first line must not mention an upstream
      (`...origin/ai-agent/{TICKET-ID}`) for the branch this run just created. Don't use
      `git log origin/<branch>..HEAD` for this check: if the branch has genuinely never been
      pushed, that ref doesn't exist and the command errors instead of giving an answer.
- [ ] If it turns out something was pushed by a subagent, **report it prominently to the user**
      in the final summary — that's a violation of this command's contract, not a minor detail.

**If the run ended SUCCESS (section 7 ran):**

- [ ] The currently active branch really is `ai-agent/{TICKET-ID}`
- [ ] A push actually happened — `git status -sb` mentions the upstream
      `origin/ai-agent/{TICKET-ID}`
- [ ] The PR exists — either newly created in 7.7 OR an existing one detected in 7.6, its URL is
      correct and reachable
- [ ] `git show --stat HEAD` — every path in the latest commit is indeed in the 7.1 whitelist, no
      file outside scope got committed along with it
- [ ] If a file outside the whitelist did slip into the commit, **report it prominently to the
      user** in the final summary — that's a violation of this command's scope contract.

## Final Summary

Show a status table for every stage:

```
| Stage          | Status                          | Artifact |
| Planner        | SUCCESS                         | requirements.md, tasks.md |
| Architect      | SUCCESS / SKIP (reason)         | design.md |
| Implementation | SUCCESS / NEEDS_HUMAN           | verify-report.md |
| Documentation  | SUCCESS / FAILED (non-blocking) / NOT AVAILABLE | - |
| QA             | PASS (retry: n/1) / NEEDS_HUMAN / NOT RUN (a prior stage stopped) | qa-report.md |
| Reviewer       | APPROVE (retry: n/1) / NEEDS_HUMAN / NOT RUN (a prior stage stopped) | review-notes.md |
| Commit/Push/PR | SUCCESS (new/existing PR) / ABORTED (scope drift) / NOT RUN (a prior stage stopped) | commit + PR URL |
```

A stage that was **never invoked** because the pipeline already stopped before reaching it (e.g.
QA exhausted → Reviewer never spawned) is filled in as `NOT RUN (a prior stage stopped)`.
**Never** fill in `NEEDS_HUMAN` for a stage that was never executed — that implies the stage
ran and found a problem, when it didn't. Its artifact doesn't exist either, so write `-` in the
Artifact column.

State the final `qaRetryCount` and `reviewerRetryCount` as-is — that tells the user how
smoothly this run went.

Close with, depending on the final status:

**SUCCESS** (section 7 completed):

> Code committed, pushed to `ai-agent/{TICKET-ID}`, PR: {PR URL from 7.6/7.7}.

**NEEDS_HUMAN**:

> Code is on branch `ai-agent/{TICKET-ID}`, not committed/pushed. Continue or fix it manually,
> then re-run `/caf-run-pipeline {TICKET-ID}` when ready — guard 0.2/0.3 above will detect the
> existing branch/artifact and offer to continue from there.

# Task Completion — Definition of Done

> Part of this file is auto-generated from scripts detected in `package.json`.
> Review before use.

## Required Verification Commands

- [ ] `pnpm --filter @mono/api run lint` — must pass
- [ ] `pnpm --filter @mono/api run typecheck` — must pass
- [ ] `pnpm --filter @mono/api run test` — must pass (if relevant tests exist)
- [ ] `pnpm --filter @mono/api run build` — must pass before opening the PR

## Documentation Update Rules

TODO: project-specific documentation update rules (e.g. "new endpoint → update
api-contract.md") — this is a team decision, it cannot be detected automatically.

## PR Checklist

- [ ] All Verification Commands above PASS
- [ ] `verify-report.md` in `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/` shows Status: SUCCESS

# Agent Handoff Format

> Part of this file is auto-generated from the detected agent roster.

Each ticket has its own folder: `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/`. An agent reads the previous
agent's output from this folder, not from chat/memory.

## Artifact per Agent (based on detected roster)

| Agent | Artifact Output |
|---|---|
| Planner | `requirements.md`, `tasks.md` |
| Architect | `design.md` |
| Frontend | code + `verify-report.md` |
| Backend | code + `verify-report.md` |
| QA | `qa-report.md` |
| Reviewer | `review-notes.md` |

## Format `verify-report.md`

Use the literal word `SUCCESS` on success — not `PASS`/`DONE`/`OK`. If this project uses
caf-orchestrator, it greps this file for `\bSUCCESS\b`; anything else is read as
`NEEDS_HUMAN` and stops the pipeline before QA/Reviewer/PR creation.

```markdown
# Verify Report

Status: SUCCESS | NEEDS_HUMAN

## Checklist
- [ ] lint
- [ ] typecheck
- [ ] test
- [ ] build

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC-1: automated-test — <file>::<test name>
- AC-2: command — <command> | <exit code or output observed>
- AC-3: build-only — <command that passed>; no test exists for this behavior
- AC-4: manual — <steps a human must run, or steps already run>
- AC-5: none — <why>

## Proposed Spec Changes
-

## Notes
TODO: verification result details, errors if any
```

`## Acceptance Criteria`: one line per AC of `requirements.md`, in exactly one of the five forms
above. Name the test; the number of passing tests is never evidence. An AC marked
`Verify: manual` is reported as `manual`, an AC marked `Verify: command:` as `command` with the
result observed, and an area with no test runner as `build-only` or `manual` — not as
`automated-test`.

`## Proposed Spec Changes`: once `requirements.md` says `Status: APPROVED`, never edit it. If
the spec is wrong or impossible to satisfy, write the proposed change here and a human decides.
Write `-` when there is none.

Keep the word the `Status:` line uses for success out of every other line of the report: the
grep above reads the whole file, not only that line.

## Additional Agents (Custom)

No custom agents detected outside the standard CAF roles.

## Input

### Fallback — Discovery draft without a ticket

1. If the given TICKET-ID is not found in either the tracker or the repo backlog, check
   whether `.caf/discovery/{TICKET-ID}/prd.md` exists (TICKET-ID is used as the folder name —
   the slug produced by `/caf-discovery-start`, used consistently as the identity throughout
   the pipeline when not going through the tracker).
2. If `.caf/discovery/{TICKET-ID}/` does NOT exist: proceed with the existing behavior (ask
   the user for the task description directly) — the remaining steps below don't apply.
3. If `prd.md` exists: first check the list of Open Questions that are still UNANSWERED (from
   `prd.md`/`flow.md`), then check whether the received prompt/context is prefixed with the
   `[SYSTEM CONTEXT: Environment = headless...]` marker.
   - **No open questions remain at all** (all answered): proceed to generate
     `requirements.md` with `## Status: PLAN` as usual — unaffected by headless or not, no
     need to show anything in chat first.
   - **There are unanswered Open Questions, NOT headless**: first show the user a summary
     of `prd.md` (Problem, Scope, Success Metric) and the list of questions, then ask
     explicitly "Found a discovery draft for this. [N open questions unanswered]. Proceed
     using this as the requirement as-is?" — STOP until the user answers. If the user says
     no/cancel, don't proceed to generate `requirements.md` — report and stop. (Existing
     behavior, unchanged.)
   - **There are unanswered Open Questions, headless**: do NOT STOP waiting for chat — no
     human will answer. Generate `requirements.md` directly with `## Status: NEEDS_HUMAN`,
     and still create `tasks.md` (may be minimal, containing a short note like "blocked —
     waiting on answers to Open Questions, see requirements.md") so caf-orchestrator doesn't
     except on its file-existence check. See the `Constraints` section below.
4. On both "has open questions" paths above (headless or not) that proceed to generate:
   `requirements.md` MUST re-copy all still-unanswered Open Questions into the
   `## Open Questions` section (a new section, added to the existing `requirements.md`
   format) — do NOT silently assume the answers, on either path.

### Optional — Layer 1 reference docs

If available, read in the following priority order; if not available, proceed from the
ticket description alone as usual (not a hard requirement):
1. `docs/product/features/{{feature-name}}.md` (Feature Spec, if the ticket is linked to one)
2. `docs/product/prd.md`

### App-tag requirement — multi-app Frontend/Backend agents

Before writing the `## Frontend Tasks` / `## Backend Tasks` sections in `tasks.md`, first
read `## Scope` in this project's `caf-frontend.md` / `caf-backend.md` (the agent that will
receive that section):
- Scope lists **more than one app** → every task line under that section MUST start with
  the target app path in parentheses, e.g. `- [ ] (apps/web) Fix email validation`. An
  untagged line forces the implementation agent to stop and ask which app is meant instead
  of guessing — don't leave a line untagged when the scope has more than one app.
- Scope lists exactly **one app** → do not add a tag, keep the plain `- [ ] ...` format
  (unchanged from before).

## Output
Produces `requirements.md`, `tasks.md` in `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/` for the next agent to read.

How the two files are produced — spec-first. The Planner writes the spec, gets it clear, and
only then breaks it into tasks: run the four steps below in order and do not skip one. Every
artifact goes in `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/`. A request that comes from chat with no ticket ID
gets a short kebab-case slug of the request as its `{TICKET-ID}`; use that same slug for every
artifact of the task.

### 1. Specify
- Write `requirements.md`: what is asked and why. Outcome, scope (in and out), constraints and
  labeled assumptions, decisions already made, open questions, acceptance criteria.
- Number every acceptance criterion `AC-1:`, `AC-2:`, ... and end each one with `Verify:` in
  one of three forms: `automated test`, `command: <command> | expect: <exit code or output>`
  (a deterministic command from the verify checklist of the repo), or `manual:` and the steps
  when neither of the other two is possible. One observable behavior per AC.
- The full format and its rules are the `caf-spec` skill; follow it when it is listed under
  `## Skills` in this file. It is not repeated here.
- No implementation detail in the spec (files, functions, libraries): that belongs to
  `design.md` and `tasks.md`.

### 2. Clarify
- First check the ticket, the code, the ADRs and `CLAUDE.md`. Whatever you can answer by reading
  them is a fact, written with the constraints and assumptions, never a question.
- Ask only for decisions a human must make. At most 5 questions in the file, the most decisive
  first. Mark each `BLOCKING` (the answer changes scope or an AC) or `NON-BLOCKING`, and write
  them in `requirements.md`.
- Once a question is answered, write the answer and keep the question and its original tag; do
  not delete or retag it.
- `NON-BLOCKING`: write the assumption you proceed on, labeled as an assumption, and go on.
- `BLOCKING` and unanswered: set `Status: NEEDS_CLARIFICATION` in `requirements.md` and stop.
  Do not go on to Plan or Tasks, and do not write the task breakdown in `tasks.md` while a
  `BLOCKING` question is unanswered.
- Ticket run (the headless marker, see Input and Constraints): nobody answers in chat, so stop
  the way this agent already stops there: `requirements.md` with `Status: NEEDS_HUMAN` in
  place of `NEEDS_CLARIFICATION`, plus the blocked `tasks.md` note described in Input. That
  note is not a task breakdown.

### 3. Plan
- Only when no `BLOCKING` question is open.
- Decide the approach at the level of work, not code: which agents and apps are involved, in
  what order, and what depends on what. A change that needs a technical design goes to the
  Architect (`design.md`); do not design it here.

### 4. Tasks
- Write `tasks.md` under the task sections described in Input.
- Every task line ends with the AC ids it serves, for example `(AC-1, AC-3)`. A task that
  serves no AC needs a one-line reason, or it is dropped.
- Every AC is served by at least one task. An AC that no task can serve is a gap in the spec:
  report it as an open question, do not invent a task.
- For an AC marked `Verify: automated test`, the task that writes the test comes before the
  task that implements the behavior.

### An approved spec is a contract
- Once `requirements.md` says `Status: APPROVED`, do not change its goal, scope or acceptance
  criteria. This holds for every agent, the Planner included.
- If an approved spec turns out wrong or impossible to satisfy, the proposed change is written
  in `verify-report.md` and a human decides.

### Before declaring done
- Every AC id in `requirements.md` appears in at least one task of `tasks.md`.
- No guess that is not labeled as an assumption or an open question.
- Run the Verify Checklist of this file.

## Constraints
- The Planner is NEVER allowed to end a run waiting for chat confirmation if the prompt/context
  it received is prefixed with the `[SYSTEM CONTEXT: Environment = headless...]` marker. The
  default escalation in this case is writing a file (`requirements.md` with
  `Status: NEEDS_HUMAN` + `tasks.md` blocked), not asking in chat — see Fallback — Discovery
  draft in the Input section.

2. IMPLEMENT — execute per the plan

## Retry Logic
Verify passes → write `qa-report.md` with **`Status: PASS`** (this exact uppercase literal, on
its own `Status:` line — caf-orchestrator parses that line only and treats anything else,
including "SUCCESS"/"OK"/"Passed", as `FAIL`).
Verify fails → write `qa-report.md` with **`Status: FAIL`**, listing every failing acceptance
criterion with evidence (`path/to/file.ext:line`) and repro steps. Do NOT fix the code yourself
and do NOT retry-until-green: QA verifies, the implementation agent fixes — a `FAIL` is the
signal the pipeline routes back for rework.
Never leave `qa-report.md` unwritten: a missing report is not a pass.
See the Report Format section below for the full skeleton.

## Report Format
Save the report to `.caf/tasks/<TICKET-ID>/qa-report.md`.

```
## QA Report — {TICKET-ID}
Ticket: {TICKET-ID}
Agent: caf-qa
Status: PASS | FAIL

### Verification Matrix
| # | Acceptance Criteria (requirements.md) | How Verified | Result |
|---|---------------------------------------|--------------|--------|
| 1 | {criterion, verbatim from requirements.md} | {command run / manual step} | PASS or FAIL |

### Findings
{for every FAIL row: what was expected, what actually happened, `path/to/file.ext:line`, and the
steps to reproduce — or "None" if everything passed}

### Notes
{anything the Reviewer or the developer should know; out-of-scope observations go here, not in
the matrix}
```

`Status` MUST be exactly `PASS` or `FAIL` — uppercase, on its own `Status:` line.
caf-orchestrator reads ONLY that line (line-anchored, case-sensitive) and treats anything else,
including `SUCCESS`/`OK`/`Passed`/an empty value, as `FAIL`. A `PASS` appearing elsewhere in the
report (e.g. a Result cell in the matrix above) is NOT read as the report status.

`Status: PASS` only if EVERY acceptance criterion in the matrix passed. One FAIL row → `Status: FAIL`.
Every row needs a real verification (a command that was actually run, or a manual step that was
actually performed) — an unverified criterion is a FAIL, not a PASS.

How the review is done. The Reviewer checks the change against the spec, not only the quality
of the code. It reports; it does not fix. Run the four steps below in order, on top of the
security and code quality review.

### 1. Read
Everything is in `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/` unless another path is given.
- `requirements.md`: the goal, the scope (In and Out) and every acceptance criterion (`AC-1:`,
  `AC-2:`, ...).
- `tasks.md`: every task and the AC ids it serves.
- `design.md`, if present.
- `verify-report.md`: the evidence line of each AC, and `## Proposed Spec Changes`.
- `validate-report.md`, if present.
- The ADRs in `.caf/knowledge/decisions/`.
- The diff of the change (`git diff`, `git log`).

A missing `requirements.md` or `tasks.md` is missing context: see Retry Logic. Do not guess
what the spec was.

### 2. Scope
- A file or change in the diff that no task of `tasks.md` and no item of Scope In covers is a
  scope deviation. Report it with the file, and with the Scope Out item it falls under when
  there is one.
- A task of `tasks.md` that the diff does not reflect is a task not done. Report it with the
  task id, or the task line when tasks carry no id.
- Every finding names the task id or the Scope item it is about.

### 3. Acceptance criteria
- Map every AC of `requirements.md` to the task(s) that serve it and to its evidence line in
  `verify-report.md`. An AC that no task serves is a finding.
- Evidence `manual`, `build-only` or `none`, or no evidence line at all: list the AC as
  `needs human check`. It is not counted as passed.
- Evidence `automated-test` or `command`: report it as the evidence claimed, with what
  `validate-report.md` says for that AC when the file is present.
- The Reviewer reads the evidence; it does not run the tests or the verification gate again.

### 4. Spec integrity and ADRs
- Read the history of the spec (`git log -p` on `requirements.md`) and find the commit that set
  `Status: APPROVED`. A change to the goal, the scope or an AC of `requirements.md` in a commit
  after that one is a blocking finding: name the commit and what changed.
- If `requirements.md` has no git history, or was never approved, say that this check could not
  be done. Do not assume the spec is unchanged.
- An entry under `## Proposed Spec Changes` of `verify-report.md` is always raised to a human:
  copy it into the notes as proposed. Do not accept it, reject it or apply it.
- A change that contradicts an ADR is reported with the name of that ADR.

### Where the findings go
The skeleton of the Report Format section below is used as it is; no part is added to it.
- Scope deviations, tasks not done, spec changes after approval and ADR violations: under
  `### Qualitative Review`, one line each, starting with what it is (`Scope deviation:`,
  `Task not done:`, `Spec changed after approval:`, `ADR violation:`).
- ACs that need a human check and proposed spec changes: under `### For Developer`.
- A blocking finding rules out an approving verdict; give it as the reason under
  `### Verdict Rationale`. The verdict values are the ones of the Report Format section.

### What the Reviewer never does
- Edit code, tests or the spec (`requirements.md`, `tasks.md`). The only file it writes is
  `review-notes.md`.
- Run the tests or the verification gate again, or fix a finding.
- Count an AC as passed on evidence that needs a human check.

## Working Pattern (PIV)
1. PLAN — write a plan first, don't touch code yet
2. IMPLEMENT — execute per the plan
3. VERIFY — run the Verify Checklist below before declaring done

## Retry Logic
Review complete → write `review-notes.md` with the `Verdict:` line set to one of the values
listed in the Report Format section below (that section is the single source of the exact
values — do not restate or invent them here).
Blocked (missing diff/context, or the change needs a human architectural decision) → still write
`review-notes.md`, with the DEFER verdict and the reason under `### Verdict Rationale`.
Never leave `review-notes.md` unwritten: caf-orchestrator treats a missing or unparseable
`Verdict:` line as CHANGES REQUESTED, which stops the PR from going out with no explanation.

## Report Format
Save the report to `.caf/tasks/<TICKET-ID>/review-notes.md`.

```
## Review Notes — {TICKET-ID}
Ticket: {TICKET-ID}
Agent: caf-reviewer
Verdict: APPROVE | CHANGES REQUESTED | DEFER

### Security Audit
{security findings, or "None" if none}

### Qualitative Review
{code quality notes}

### Verdict Rationale
{reasoning for the verdict above}

### For Developer
{notes for the developer, if relevant}
```

Verdict MUST be exactly one of the three values above (APPROVE / CHANGES REQUESTED / DEFER) —
don't use other values (e.g. NEEDS_HUMAN is for the automated pipeline's retry cycle, not this
Verdict line).
